messages:
zoe: FYI deploy-bot stopped the global rollout for release/3.8.2 during pre-prod checks. It flagged an SBOM provenance mismatch + a medium transitive vuln. Need quick triage: emergency patch, scoped canary, or rollback to 3.8.1. please respond with evidence + proposed owner for rollback.

ben: quick context 1 build+smoke passed. canary started but halted by policy. what does the provenance mismatch look like?

hiro: pasted from deploy-bot below. looks like the signed SBOM references a different build id than the container digest (probable CI signing race). vuln is transitive `libwebp` CVE-2020-7777 score 5.4.

deploy-bot: compliance: sbom-provenance-check/4682223400 FAILED
- artifact: gcr.io/redwood/release/3.8.2-canary@sha256:fa12be34
- sbom: sbom-3.8.2-canary.json (signed)
- provenance: SBOM.provenance.build_id != artifact.build_id (expected fa12be34, found fa12be35)

vuln-scan-staging/4682223401: 1 medium (libwebp 1.2.0) - CVE-2020-7777 - exploitability low

security-bot: policy: provenance-mismatch -> block by default. Exception path: must provide audit log showing signing key used + CI run id, and a mitigation note.

ben: that provenance mismatch is worrying. could be a CI race or a fresh rebuild slipped in. we should avoid silent roll-forwards.

zoe: options: (A) quick audit to prove SBOM signed by the canonical CI run (owner: hiro), (B) scoped EU-only canary under exception, (C) rollback to 3.8.1. Timebox 30m. rollback owner if chosen: @ben.

hiro: running `ci/audit-signing` now (job id: audit-468222). will paste logs.

ops-pager: NOTE: rollback playbook `releases/rollback-quick` -> runbook v2.3, estimated 6-10m for revert & traffic switch. pager watch: releases-oncall.

hiro: audit logs: `ci-run-id: 2026-03-21-1145`, signer key id `redwood-ci-key-2`, cosign log: signature applied to sbom for build fa12be34 at 11:46:12Z. Another CI re-run produced artifact fa12be35 at 11:47:05Z. Evidence attached: https://artifacts.internal/prov/audit-468222.txt

ben: so SBOM was signed for fa12be34 but the pushed image is fa12be35. that's a mismatch. but we have the audit trail showing the signing key was correct and a subsequent rebuild caused the digest bump.

security-bot: conditional exception template: require signed SBOM link, audit log link, mitigation note, rollback owner, and monitoring hook for 2h.

zoe: mitigation note draft: `SBOM signed for build fa12be34; image fa12be35 is a non-functional rebuild (no code changes) from CI retry. Verified via CI logs. Transitive vuln (libwebp CVE-2020-7777) low exploitability; runtime IDS active. Patch targeted in 3.8.3 within 14 days.`

ben: i can own rollback if needed. recommend scoped canary in US-east only (25% traffic) under exception while we push a rebuild with matching provenance.

hiro: i can trigger a rebuild that reproduces the signed build id (force-id build) and re-run signing. ETA ~12m.

deploy-bot: attestation present for sbom-3.8.2-canary.json (cosign sig path: s3://redwood-artifacts/attestations/3.8.2-canary/cosign.sig)
artifact digest: sha256:fa12be35
sbom hash: sha256:bb33cc44ddeeff00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff00112233445566778899

security-bot: exception granted for scoped canary (US-east, 25% traffic) provided:
- audit link: https://artifacts.internal/prov/audit-468222.txt
- signed SBOM link: s3://redwood-artifacts/attestations/3.8.2-canary/cosign.sig
- mitigation note in release docs
- rollback owner assigned: ben
- monitoring: 2h window

zoe: decision: proceed with scoped US-east canary now. hiro will rebuild and produce a matching signed SBOM; if rebuild completes within 30m we'll replace the canary artifact with prov-matching image and promote. if not, we keep the scoped canary under watch and plan rollback at 2h if any anomaly. ben is rollback owner.

ben: setting PagerDuty watch and alert thresholds (error-rate > 0.8% or anomaly in IDS).

hiro: kicking off forced rebuild `ci/rebuild --force-id=fa12be34` now. ETA ~12m. will post link to new attestation when done.

deploy-bot: action: canary rollout -> US-east (25% traffic), start_ts 4682226000

zoe: thanks all. logging SEC ticket SEC-6022 and updating release notes with mitigation + links. we'll reconvene in this thread if anything changes.
